extracted.intended_audience: Heads of executive departments and agencies; agency legislative drafters and staff preparing proposed legislation or reports to OMB on extensions of criminal law enforcement authority
extracted.subtask_short: legislation extending agency law enforcement authority
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for evaluating or drafting proposed legislation or reports that would extend criminal law enforcement authorities to Federal agencies, specifying when and under what conditions particular powers may be granted. Intended to guide agencies in preparing submissions to OMB and to ensure consistent, limited expansion of enforcement powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Policy — need for authority (Section 4.a)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should not have criminal law enforcement authority unless the agency's ability to perform an essential function within its jurisdiction is significantly hampered by its lack of criminal law enforcement authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To assess need, consider scope of agency jurisdiction, nature of essential functions (administrative vs. investigative/protective), and whether lack of authority significantly impairs performance of essential statutory responsibilities. Mere existence of criminal sanctions in statutes does not alone justify enforcement powers; civil or administrative remedies are preferred where appropriate. The agency must demonstrate that lack of authority significantly impairs an essential function.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Policy — availability of assistance from traditional agencies (Section 4.b)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency's need for law enforcement authority should be denied if that need can be met effectively by assistance from law enforcement agencies with such authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider alternatives such as assistance from the FBI or Secret Service, temporary designation of special duty agents of the Department of Justice, or a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) specifying when and how assistance will be rendered. Factors: kind of assistance required, duration, willingness and ability of traditional agencies to assist given jurisdictional limits, priorities, and resources, and legal basis for conferring special agent status. Only if a satisfactory MOU or other arrangement cannot ensure timely and effective assistance should the agency be granted authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Policy — adequate safeguards (Section 4.c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequate safeguards must exist to ensure proper exercise of the authority by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safeguards refer to training, supervision, and oversight. Agencies must ensure employees authorized to exercise law enforcement powers receive necessary training, are supervised pursuant to policies and procedures approved by the Attorney General, and are subject to effective oversight within the Executive branch and by appropriate congressional committees. Agencies should prepare an annual brief statistical summary of their use of the law enforcement powers granted to facilitate oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Policy — net advantage (Section 4.d)
rubrics_metrics.description: The advantages attributable to the agency's possession of the authority must reasonably be expected to exceed the disadvantages likely to result from its exercise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh risks such as interference with traditional law enforcement (coordination difficulties, jurisdictional intrusion, conflicting operations), potential to prejudice prosecutions, and misuse leading Congress to restrict powers elsewhere. Consider monetary costs (training, equipment, benefits, duplication), potential slackening of non-criminal enforcement efforts, FOIA/Privacy Act burdens, and civil liberties concerns. Balance these against benefits: improved mission performance, recruitment/retention, and relief of burdens on traditional agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to Carry a Firearm (Section 5.a)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should not authorize employees to carry firearms unless specific conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required conditions: (1) significant likelihood employees will face situations in which lawful use of a firearm is permitted to (i) protect themselves from imminent death, serious bodily injury, or kidnapping; (ii) prevent another from causing imminent death/bodily injury/kidnapping to a person under their protection; or (iii) prevent imminent loss/destruction of property of substantial value under their protection; (2) it is unlikely timely and effective assistance will be available from another agency; (3) the employee has completed an accredited course of training in carrying and use of firearms and is currently qualified (including periodic reevaluation and firing-range proficiency checks); and (4) the agency will establish AG-approved policies and procedures to prevent unauthorized use or misuse, including case-by-case approval of an employee's authority to carry by a designated senior official. Guidance includes examples (arrest/search duties, protective assignments, protection of property critical to national security) and cautions (do not arm on mere convenience or speculative need).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to Seek and Execute an Arrest or Search Warrant (Section 5.b)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should not permit employees to seek and execute arrest or search warrants except with limits and required conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority should be limited to arrest/searches for offenses within the agency's jurisdiction or involving resistance to the employee's authority, and does not include authorization for electronic surveillance (see covert techniques). Required conditions mirror firearm criteria: (1) significant likelihood employees will frequently need to make such arrests or searches; (2) timely and effective assistance from another agency is unlikely; (3) employees have completed an accredited course in execution of arrest and search warrants; and (4) agency will establish AG-approved policies and procedures to prevent unauthorized use or misuse. Consider alternatives such as administrative subpoenas, and factors like location of search, nature of items to be seized, need for special expertise, and time required to complete searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to Make a Warrantless Arrest (Section 5.c)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should not authorize warrantless arrests except when limited to arrests of persons who committed felonies (probable cause) or misdemeanors committed in the employee's presence, and when specified conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required conditions: (1) significant likelihood employees will frequently encounter situations requiring prompt arrest rather than waiting for warrants (examples: immediate threats to persons/property, risk of escape, destruction of evidence, or thwarting duties); (2) timely and effective assistance from another agency is unlikely; (3) employee has completed accredited arrest training; and (4) agency will establish AG-approved policies/procedures for preventing unlawful or inappropriate use (training, supervision, oversight). If authorized, attendant authority to conduct a search incident to arrest is implied. The guideline recognizes federal employees' need to act in emergencies and protects them regarding state laws on citizens' arrests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to Serve Grand Jury Subpoenas or Other Legal Process (Section 5.d)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should not permit employees to serve grand jury subpoenas, summonses, court orders, or other legal process unless specified conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A less rigorous standard applies than for arrests/searches: authority may be granted when service can be made more conveniently or expeditiously by the employee than by another agency. Factors: probable effectiveness of administrative subpoenas, time constraints, employee familiarity with the person/location to be served, and anticipated difficulties in making service. Required conditions include (1) significant likelihood employees will frequently need to serve such process; (2) that service cannot be made conveniently/expeditiously by another agency; (3) employee training in service of process; and (4) agency AG-approved policies/procedures to prevent unauthorized use or misuse. If danger to the employee exists during service and the employee is not armed, assistance should be sought from an agency with firearms authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to Administer an Oath or Affirmation (Section 5.e)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may be authorized to permit employees to administer oaths or affirmations when it is necessary or desirable to take sworn statements or testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Less stringent standard because the power is unlikely to be intrusive or harmful. Required conditions: (1) significant likelihood employees will frequently need to take sworn statements/testimony; (2) it is unlikely that oaths or affirmations can be administered as conveniently/expeditiously by another agency; (3) employee has been trained in requirements for administering oaths/affirmations (training need not be from an accredited course); and (4) agency will establish AG-approved policies/procedures to prevent unauthorized use or misuse. This authority may be granted when desirable as well as strictly necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to Use a Covert Investigative Technique (Section 5.f)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should not permit use of covert investigative techniques (electronic surveillance, undercover operations, paid informants, or other clandestine methods) except under the most compelling circumstances and with strong guarantees against misuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required considerations: (1) significant likelihood employees will frequently need to use the technique in performing duties; (2) timely and effective assistance from an agency with expertise is unlikely; (3) employee has completed an accredited course of training in the technique; and (4) agency will establish AG-approved policies/procedures (including requirement that each use be approved on a case-by-case basis by a designated senior official) to prevent unauthorized use or even appearance of misuse. Additional guidance: because of secrecy and potential for abuse, high-level approval is required; promises to witnesses (e.g., non-prosecution assurances, favorable sentencing recommendations, witness protection participation) involve prosecutorial judgment and investigators should not be given independent authority to make such promises except when specifically authorized by the prosecutor.
